main_text.p: nem sumti, hoc breuiter monere libet, Vt corporis lasciuiam, inedia & ieiunio domari: sic eiusdem fastum nimiumq; cultum, uili operimento non parum minui. Cultus, inquit ille, & victus familiaris uitam indicant. Itaque utriusq; habenda ratio est ijs, qui uita & mores serio emendare student. Sordidae, inquit Hieronymus, ueftes, candidae mentis indicia sunt. Hau ddubie autem sordidas dixit, nō pretiosas nimium. His enim cur nonnulli utantur, uere docuit Gregorius, cuius haec uerba sunt: Quòd pro sola inani gloria ueftimetum pretiosius quaeritur, res ipsa teftatur: quia nemo uult ibi pretiosis uestibus indui, ubi ab alijs nō posfit uideri.

Caeterum saccus primum humilitatis index erat: quia cultus & ornatus, eo sum to uefteq; mutata, corpori detrahitur: deinde, signum reatus & doloris. Luc. 10. 13. Vae tibi Corazin: uae tibi Beth-saida, nam siin Tyro & Sidonae editae fuissent uirtutes quae editae sunt apud uos, olim cum facco & cinere sedentes resipuissent.
Abfit autem superstitio & magnificentia nimia a fidelium habitu, qui debet esse ἐσθῆτι σεμνῆς; & habeatur decori ratio. Etsi enim

page.notes: Printed text is in roman type with some italic. Words are copied as printed, including the original spellings. The page is only lightly foxed. Doubtful readings: "Hau ddubie" appears as printed with a space and may be a printer's break; "Abfit" line and the Greek word after "esse" are read with uncertainty. The Greek in the last line is partly obscured by a stain and is copied as best I can read it. Catchword "enim" at the foot right has been placed in the final paragraph and should be treated as the start of the next line. A signature mark "§ 5" appears at the foot left.
